newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL pushing for single north Alberta pipe.
newsitem.headline: IPL pushing for single north Alberta pipe.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line is in talks with northern Alberta oil sands operators with the aim of combining numerous pipeline proposals from the region into one, Interprovincial President Pat Daniel said on Thursday.
Daniel told reporters his company was spearheading negotiations to build one pipeline, which would cost between C$300 million and C$350 million, instead of at least four that have now been proposed.

Companies besides IPL that have said they may apply to build pipelines to Edmonton or Hardisty, Alberta from the Athabasca region include Suncor Energy Inc, Alberta Energy Co Ltd and Shell Canada Ltd. All are expanding oil sands and heavy oil operations or are planning new projects.
Daniel said initial capacity of a "broader solution" pipeline would be between 350,000 and 500,000 barrels a day to accomodate a spate of new development.
He said a key participant would be Suncor, whose own pipeline plans were more advanced than the other firms' because of expansion progress at its oil sands plant north of Fort McMurray, Alberta.
